channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: CIS Conference Discusses Generation Z Mental Health and Future Impact
item.description: An international conference on the mental health of Generation Z was held, initiated by Kyrgyzstan. Representatives from Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, and Tajikistan participated. Discussions focused on current youth challenges, the need for adult support, empathy, and open communication.

item.title: Kyrgyz Parliament Committee Approves $60 Million EDB Loan for Osh Oblast Water Supply
item.description: A Kyrgyz Parliament committee approved a $60 million loan agreement with the Eurasian Development Bank (EDB) for improving water supply and sanitation in 32 villages in Osh Oblast. The project aims to provide safe drinking water to over 178,000 residents.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Only 28% of Childhood Cancers Detected at Early Stages in 2025
item.description: In 2025, only 28% of pediatric oncological and hematological diseases in Uzbekistan were diagnosed at early stages, according to Health Minister Eldor Adilov. This marks an increase from 23% in 2023, with new cases rising by 62.4%.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's GDP projected to exceed 2.7 trillion soms by 2027
item.description: The volume of Kyrgyzstan's GDP is projected to exceed 2.736 trillion soms by 2027, according to Adylbek Kasymaliev. He presented the draft republican budget for 2027 at a parliamentary committee meeting. The consolidated budget's total resources are planned at 1.053 trillion soms.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman sign strategic partnership agreement, plan new bank
item.description: Uzbekistan and Oman have signed a strategic partnership agreement aimed at elevating relations and cooperation. Over 30 documents were exchanged, including those on visa-free travel, industrial cooperation, and finance. Agreements also cover the creation of a new commercial bank in Uzbekistan with Omani participation.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Lower Mortgage Down Payment to 10% by 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Industry and Construction, in collaboration with Otbasy Bank, is developing mechanisms to reduce the initial mortgage down payment to 10%. Specific proposals are expected to be presented in 2027. The initiative aims to make housing loans more accessible to citizens.

item.title: RG Brands Kazakhstan Reports Significant Losses After PepsiCo Contract Ends
item.description: RG Brands Kazakhstan has reported a net loss of 13.16 billion tenge for Q3 2026, a stark contrast to a profit of 13.01 billion tenge in the same period of 2025, following the expiration of its contract with PepsiCo. Revenue dropped by 40.9% to 84.92 billion tenge.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman Sign Mutual Visa Exemption Agreement
item.description: Uzbekistan and Oman have signed a mutual visa exemption agreement. The document was adopted following high-level negotiations in Muscat, in the presence of President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Sultan Haitham bin Tarik Al Said. This agreement aims to enhance bilateral relations between the two countries.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman Sign Over 30 Bilateral Documents, Including Strategic Partnership
item.description: Uzbekistan and Oman have signed over 30 bilateral documents following high-level talks in Muscat, including a strategic partnership agreement that elevates relations to a new level. Agreements were also reached on mutual visa exemption, industrial cooperation, preferential trade, and various other sectors.

item.title: Bishkek accounts for 60% of Kyrgyzstan's 2 trillion som trade turnover
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's domestic trade turnover neared 1.9 trillion som in the first ten months of 2026, with Bishkek dominating 60.2% of the total. Retail trade grew to 723 billion som, while wholesale saw a slight decrease. Bishkek led with 1.137 trillion som.

item.title: UN OCHA: Taliban Restrictions Impact Women's Access to Essential Services
item.description: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reports that Taliban restrictions are hindering women's participation in humanitarian work and their access to essential services and aid, including hygiene items. These limitations are disrupting humanitarian response efforts in Afghanistan.

item.title: Kazakhstan Reports 28 Cases of Meningococcal Infection This Year
item.description: Since the beginning of 2026, 28 cases of meningococcal infection have been confirmed in Kazakhstan, with 78.5% of those infected being children under 14. The Ministry of Health noted a 2.2-fold decrease in infections compared to the same period in 2025. Cases have been detected in ten regions.

item.title: Astana's Appearance to Change Under New Facade Design Rules
item.description: Astana has officially approved new city design code rules for facades. Building exteriors, advertisements, and storefronts will be strictly regulated by a special administrator. Owners must obtain facade passports, which detail where signs and structures can be placed, or face legal action.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Qajet Taxi App to Integrate Domestic Digital Maps and Navigation
item.description: Kazakhstan's Qajet taxi service plans to use domestic digital maps and navigation technologies. The Ministry of Digital Development aims to test state geoportals within a commercial platform. This integration will improve address search, geocoding, and routing accuracy for passenger transport and delivery services.

item.title: Teenager Driving Without License Causes Fatal Accident in Uzbekistan
item.description: A 13-year-old boy died after a car crash in Uzbekistan's Samarkand region. The vehicle, driven by an unlicensed teenager, son of a traffic police officer, veered off the road and hit a tree. Two other teenagers were hospitalized with injuries.

item.title: Spanish Firm Roca to Produce Toilets and Sinks in Kazakhstan
item.description: Spanish company Roca, a global leader in sanitary ware, plans to start producing toilets and sinks in Kazakhstan's Kyzylorda region. Vice Minister Olzhas Saparkhanov stated the new plant will partially meet domestic demand, though not fully satisfy it.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Presents Draft National Budget for 2027 and Forecasts for 2028-2029
item.description: The draft national budget for 2027 and forecasts for 2028-2029 were presented to the Jogorku Kenesh by Cabinet Chairman Adylbek Kasymaliev. In January-October 2026, national budget revenues exceeded the plan by 27.9 billion soms. The primary focus remains on ensuring long-term economic growth while fulfilling social obligations.

item.title: Bishkek Allocates 500 Million Soms for New Bus Procurement
item.description: Bishkek plans to purchase approximately 1,500 additional public transport units to address a shortage of buses, especially during peak hours. The city has allocated 500 million soms from the local budget for this purpose, with an agreement already signed. Sixty-five short buses are expected by January 20. The need for additional transport extends to Chuy region districts.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Prime Minister Attends Parliamentary Committee Meeting on Budgetary Legislation
item.description: Prime Minister Adylbek Kasymaliev participated in an expanded committee meeting of the Jogorku Kenesh (parliament) discussing crucial budgetary draft laws for the country's socio-economic development. He highlighted the productive cooperation between the Cabinet of Ministers and the Parliament, emphasizing the importance of citizen-focused legislation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan: Naryn Region Sees Development in Housing, Transport, and Energy
item.description: Over the past five years, Naryn region in Kyrgyzstan has implemented several development projects in housing, transport, energy, and culture. New facilities include a modern cultural center, apartment buildings, and the completion of the Balykchy-Kochkor railway. The Kulanak HPP and solar-powered lighting on the Bishkek-Naryn-Torugart road are also noted.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Banking Assets Exceed 1.4 Trillion Som, Loans Grow Nearly 30%
item.description: As of September 30, 2026, Kyrgyzstan's banking sector assets reached 1.425 trillion som, a 17.7% increase year-to-date. The loan portfolio grew by 29.9% to 658.7 billion som. Islamic financing saw the highest growth at 64.2%. Deposits increased by 5.3% to 912.3 billion som.

item.title: UN Chief Urges Faster Action to End Global Conflicts and Ensure Aid Delivery
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres called for more prompt measures to end ongoing armed conflicts, particularly in Gaza, Ukraine, and Sudan. He stressed the need for humanitarian aid delivery and combating climate change. Guterres highlighted the severe humanitarian suffering caused by conflicts and the unacceptable scale of the crisis in Myanmar.

item.title: UN Demands Release of Kazakh Journalist Duman Mukhammedkarim
item.description: The United Nations has demanded the release of Kazakh journalist Duman Mukhammedkarim. The specific reasons for the demand and the circumstances surrounding his detention were not detailed in the provided information.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Introduce Electronic Medical Policies and Expand Free Drug List
item.description: Uzbekistan has approved a comprehensive healthcare reform plan for 2027-2031, including the introduction of electronic medical policies and an expanded list of free medications. By 2031, the state medical insurance system aims to cover all households, with electronic policies available via the my.gov.uz portal.

item.title: EU's Borrell Calls Russian Demands in Ukraine Talks 'Absurd'
item.description: EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs Josep Borrell described Russia's demands in negotiations with Ukraine as 'absurd,' stating they are a pretext for continuing the war. He emphasized that the EU must realistically assess the situation and prepare counter-demands, noting Russia's failure to adhere to existing security agreements.

item.title: Kazakhstan Clarifies Responsibility for Traffic Fines on Leased Vehicles
item.description: Kazakhstan's Vice Minister of Industry and Construction, Olzhas Saparbekov, has clarified that the lessee is responsible for paying traffic fines incurred on leased vehicles. Amendments to by-laws have resolved previous disputes regarding fine payments, ensuring clear division of responsibility between leasing companies and users.

item.title: Afghan Leader Akhundzada Urges Unity and Protection of Islamic Emirate
item.description: Sheikh Hibatullah Akhundzada, the Supreme Leader of the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan, has called for unity and the protection of the current political system. Speaking at Kabul University, he stated he would not allow Muslims to fight amongst themselves to preserve his authority and emphasized the importance of promoting Islamic teachings.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Demands Guaranteed Sales for Domestic Producers
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to launch approximately 200 new industrial enterprises by year-end, totaling 1.7 trillion tenge. Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has instructed officials to ensure stable demand, access to financing, and fair competition for domestic manufacturers, emphasizing the priority of developing local production and protecting the internal market.

item.title: Taliban Leader Reaffirms Authority, Emphasizes Obedience to 'Amir'
item.description: Taliban religious scholars renewed their allegiance to the group's leader, Mullah Hibatullah Akhundzada, at a gathering in Kabul University. Akhundzada, speaking via media, stressed the importance of obedience to the 'Amir,' stating that Islamic law cannot be implemented without leadership. He also asserted that judicial punishments, including executions, require his explicit order.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Emphasizes Prioritizing Domestic Products in Budget Spending
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov stated that when budget funds are allocated, the company utilizing them and the materials purchased must be domestic. He stressed that importing goods when domestic alternatives exist contradicts national interests. Approximately 200 new industrial enterprises are planned for launch this year.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Sees Significant Price Increases in Hotels and Public Catering Since Year Start
item.description: Hotel prices in Kyrgyzstan have risen by 25.7% and public catering services by 23.2% since the beginning of the year. Overall consumer prices increased by 8.1% by September, with services rising faster than goods. Transport services increased by 13.5%.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Fines and License Suspensions for Aggressive Road Behavior
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering imposing fines of 10,000 soms and temporary license suspensions for drivers and passengers engaging in aggressive road altercations. Repeat offenders within a year could face a six-month driving ban. The proposed legislation aims to curb dangerous behavior on the roads.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Transition to New Economic Growth Model from 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to adopt a new economic growth model starting in 2027, focusing on increasing added value, implementing new technologies, and creating high-paying jobs. The goal is to double export volumes and expand the middle class.

item.title: France's Societe Generale Bank to Open Representative Office in Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank has accredited the representative office of France's Societe Generale bank. The office aims to study the country's financial market and expand cooperation with state bodies, financial institutions, and the private sector. Founded in 1864, Societe Generale is a leading European banking and financial group operating in 58 countries.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Simplifying Disability Confirmation for Adults
item.description: A bill in Kyrgyzstan proposes simplifying the process of confirming disability for individuals over 18 who were previously recognized as children with disabilities. The amendments also aim to extend social benefits for up to three months if re-examinations are delayed by state bodies. The simplified procedure would apply to cases with documented persistent and irreversible health impairments.

item.title: Dushanbe to Host First Tajikistan Coal Industry Forum in December 2026
item.description: Dushanbe will host the first International Forum of Tajikistan's Coal Industry in December 2026, according to the Ministry of Industry and New Technologies. The forum aims to develop the sector, attract investment, and introduce modern technologies.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Tax Revenues Grow, But Borrowing Remains Necessary
item.description: Despite accelerating tax revenue growth, Kazakhstan's budget still requires borrowing. Tax revenues increased by 18.5% in the first nine months of 2026, driven by legislative changes and favorable commodity prices. However, significant budget obligations necessitate continued debt financing.

item.title: Uzbekistan Faces Widespread Housing Scams, Thousands of Buyers Affected
item.description: Thousands of homebuyers in Uzbekistan have been victims of problematic housing projects, with losses totaling billions of soms. Recent cases involve construction companies accused of fraud, building without permits, and failing to meet deadlines. Authorities are investigating multiple developers for alleged deception and mismanagement of funds.

item.title: Chinese Companies Propose Overpriced Irrigation Projects in Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan's Water Resources Minister, Shavkat Khamrayev, addressed delays in irrigation reconstruction projects with Chinese companies. A parliamentary member noted that some projects, including a $130 million initiative in several regions involving a Chinese bank, have not yet commenced. Chinese firms reportedly proposed costs more than double the expected price.

item.title: Taliban Official Calls Power Concentration a 'Blessing', Rejects Inclusive Government
item.description: A senior Taliban official, Chief Justice Abdul Hakim Haqqani, described the concentration of power within the group as a "blessing," arguing that power-sharing would have strengthened opposition forces. His remarks at a gathering in Kabul suggest the Taliban views inclusive governance as detrimental to their control, rather than a solution to Afghanistan's crisis.
